name: Bali 1928: A Musical Journey Back in Time at Desa Potato Head
location: Desa Potato Head
description: Bali’s extraordinary and otherworldly culture was once the island’s most enticing allure. Before beaches and resorts, it was dance, art, music and ceremony that captured the imagination – a vibrant way of life that intertwined nature and ritual into the everyday. The year was 1928, and such was this cultural fascination that German record labels Odeon and Beka sent engineers to Bali to capture a sound quite like anything they had heard before: the rhythmic reverberations of the gamelan, and the ethereal voices of Balinese song. Around this time, pioneering researchers like the ethnomusicologist Colin McPhee, artist and author Miguel Covarrubias, and art collector Rolf de Maré captured silent film footage of ceremonies, dancers and everyday life. For decades these lay in archives, unseen and unheard by those depicted. Fast forward to 2013. Dr. Edward Herbst, Arbiter of Cultural Traditions New York, together with ITB STIKON Bali, began a repatriation project, Arsip Bali 1928 , scoping the world for these recordings and bringing them back to Bali.

JULIA TIPSY Grooves, grooves and probably a few more grooves. SoFi Flying the Swiss flag and bringing a little Alpine mischief to the tropics. name: Padma Musical Series: George Harliono & Hera Hyesang Park
location: Padma Resort Legian
description: The Padma Musical Series returns this December with an evening of classical music featuring two acclaimed international artists: British-Indonesian pianist George Harliono and Korean soprano Hera Hyesang Park. Returning to Bali following his previous appearance at Padma Resort Legian, Harliono has established an impressive international career from a remarkably young age. In 2023, he received the Silver Medal at the XVII International Tchaikovsky Competition, one of the most prestigious events in the classical music world. His performance history includes celebrated venues such as Wigmore Hall, Royal Albert Hall, Berlin Philharmonie Kammermusiksaal and Suntory Hall, alongside appearances with orchestras including the NHK Symphony Orchestra, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra and Mariinsky Orchestra. Joining him for the December performance is Hera Hyesang Park, making her Bali debut. A Deutsche Grammophon recording artist and graduate of The Juilliard School, the Korean soprano has performed at leading opera houses and concert halls around the world, including the Metropolitan Opera, Staatsoper Berlin, Paris Opéra and Glyndebourne Festival. Her repertoire spans celebrated works including La bohème , La traviata , Don Giovanni and Le nozze di Figaro . Her debut album, I Am Hera , was released in 2020, followed by Breathe , which received the 2024 Opus Klassik Award for Videoclip of the Year.
